name: Induction Hardening
desc: Hardness exactly where a component wears, and nowhere else. A shaped copper coil heats the surface to austenitising temperature in seconds while the core stays comparatively cool, so the running face transforms to martensite and the body keeps the toughness it started with. Shafts, gears, journals, splines, cam lobes and rolls up to 700 mm diameter by 1500 mm long. Coils are designed and fabricated in-house, including flux concentrators, which is what holds case depth to tolerance on profiles an off-the-shelf coil cannot follow. It moves a part far less than a furnace cycle, so it often suits finished or near-finished components. Send the drawing and the specified case depth and we will confirm it before the job is booked.

name: Hardening & Tempering
desc: Hardening and tempering are a pair, and running one without the other is how components fail. Heating above the critical temperature and quenching transforms the structure to martensite, which is hard and wear-resistant and also brittle enough to crack under shock. Tempering afterwards brings the toughness back and sets the final hardness. Oil quenching in a 30,000 litre tank, on components up to six metres long. Hardness is verified in our own laboratory, on the same floor as the furnaces, before the part is released.

name: Heat Treatment
desc: Fifteen furnaces across five configurations, all rated to 1200 C, from 800 mm pit furnaces to six-metre gas-fired box furnaces, with a 30,000 litre oil quench. That range matters for one simple reason: a part cut down to fit the furnace is a part that has been compromised. Whatever the drawing calls the operation, hardening, tempering, annealing, normalising, stress relieving or solution annealing, every batch runs a documented, repeatable cycle with full traceability, from a single prototype to a production run.

name: Annealing
desc: Annealing is the step that makes the next operation possible. Heating above the critical temperature and cooling slowly softens the material, releases internal stress and restores the ductility that cold work or an earlier heat treatment has used up. It is usually not the finish; it is what lets the part be machined, formed or drawn without cracking or springing out of tolerance. Components up to six metres long.

name: Normalising
desc: Normalising heats the material above its critical temperature and then cools it in still air, leaving a finer and more uniform grain than the part arrived with. That is what makes everything after it more predictable: machining, further heat treatment, and the way the component behaves in service. Commonly specified for castings, forgings and weldments, where the as-produced structure is coarse or uneven. Components up to six metres long.

name: Stress Relieving
desc: Welding, machining and casting all lock stress inside a component, and stress that is never released will find its own way out later, as distortion on the machine bed or a crack in service. Stress relieving heats the part below its critical temperature and holds it there long enough for that stress to redistribute, then cools it slowly. Because it stays below critical, hardness and mechanical properties are retained. Welded fabrications, machined and cast components up to six metres long.

name: Solution Annealing
desc: Solution annealing returns a stainless steel or a superalloy to the condition it is supposed to be in. The part is heated until the precipitates that formed during welding or prior processing dissolve back into the matrix, then quenched quickly enough that they have no chance to re-form on the way down. That is what restores corrosion resistance in a sensitised weld zone and puts the alloy back into a known, specified condition.

name: Flame Hardening
desc: Some components are simply too large, too heavy or too awkward to put in a furnace or inside an induction coil. Flame hardening takes the heat to the part instead: a controlled oxy-gas flame raises the working surface to austenitising temperature and a quench follows immediately behind it, hardening the face while the body stays as it was. Large gears, rings, tracks, slideways and wear faces, including work on components a coil cannot encircle.

name: Inductor Manufacturing
desc: Custom induction coils, designed and built in-house. The coil is the tool that decides where the heat goes, how deep it reaches and how evenly it spreads around a component, and a coil that nearly fits produces a case that nearly meets the drawing. We shape the coil to the part rather than compromising the part to a coil that already exists, and use flux concentrators to steer the field on gear teeth, splines and internal bores, which is what makes single-tooth and contour hardening practical. Coils are brazed to the profile the work requires. If you run your own induction equipment and need a coil built or replaced, send the part drawing and the machine details and we will quote against them.

name: Material Testing
desc: Heat treatment without verification is an assumption. Our laboratory sits on the same floor as the furnaces, which means hardness, mechanical properties and internal soundness are confirmed on the treated part before it is released. Mechanical testing on a 40 tonne universal testing machine, Brinell and Rockwell hardness, and non-destructive testing by ultrasonic, magnetic particle and dye penetrant methods. Every figure that appears on a certificate traces back to an in-house measurement. Testing is also available as a standalone service.
